A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Planned Diffusion and contain readable main text, equations, figures, and appendices. The shared method and experiments can be matched despite substantial reorganization and renamed attention variants.

before.justification: V1 reports original AlpacaEval quality and latency measurements, training-epoch comparisons, control-tag ablations, and inference-parameter sweeps.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds evaluated baselines, speedup distributions, source-level results, and qualitative success and failure cases.

M1.justification: Both attention variants already exist in v1: PD-DA becomes PD in v2, while the original sparse PD becomes PDSA. The planner, hybrid training loss, control tags, entropy-based denoising, and caching procedure are retained. The expanded denoising-order formalism does not establish a new implemented method.

E1.justification: Both versions train on annotated SlimOrca and evaluate instruction following on AlpacaEval. Appendix F breaks down existing AlpacaEval sources rather than introducing five new evaluation datasets. The qualitative examples remain within instruction-following coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Section 5, Figure 2, and Table 1 add actual comparisons with Pasta-SFT and Skeleton-of-Thought, which v1 only discusses or cites. This substantially strengthens comparison with competing semantic-parallelism methods. An AR reference also appears in the revised quality-latency sweep.

E3.justification: The primary training, inference, and LCWR protocols remain unchanged. Section 6 now reports four-epoch ablations under the dense-PD definition rather than v1's sparse-PD definition. New supplementary analyses use 803 speedup samples and source-group counts totaling 801, without explaining exclusions from the 805-prompt benchmark. Pasta is expressly evaluated with SFT rather than RL.

E4.justification: V2 adds analyses of per-instruction speedup variation, sensitivity to instruction source, and successful versus failed semantic planning in Appendices C, F, and G. These substantially extend the original aggregate comparisons and parameter sweeps. Section 6 also revises the control-tag ablation, including the synchronization finding.

E5.justification: V2 Table 2 newly reports source-level LCWR with standard errors. Appendix C adds a standard deviation of 4.10 for speedup ratios across instructions; this measures sample heterogeneity, not repeated-run uncertainty. Neither version reports random seeds or repeated-run counts, and v2 does not explain its standard-error estimation procedure.

E6.justification: V2 adds Pasta-SFT results of 5.740 s and 26.13% LCWR, and Skeleton-of-Thought results of 3.101 s and 40.72% (Table 1), plus distribution, subgroup, and qualitative findings. The no-sync ablation changes from 39.4% at 2.08 s to 42.96% at 5.81 s under the revised variant definition; this is not a same-setting improvement. Existing headline results are retained after matching renamed variants.

T1.justification: V2 Sections 3–4 introduce ordered partitions, conditional factorization, uniform and entropy-based orders, and composition of within-chunk orders into a planned order. This replaces v1's main span-independence formulation with a substantially expanded mathematical account. Equation 3 also gains a 1/t factor, and Section 5 adds an attention-cost and critical-path complexity argument.

C1.justification: V2 recasts the central contribution as learning a denoising order and specifies the headline Pareto-frontier claim for parallel generation with discrete diffusion. The single-model hybrid novelty and 1.27–1.81× speedup claims remain. Training-compute scaling becomes an explicit introductory contribution but was already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: V1 recommends removing synchronization for latency-sensitive settings; v2 concludes that removal provides no latency benefit in its revised ablation. Appendix G newly explains how generic planning topics can cause repetitive outputs, qualifying planning reliability. Appendices C and F interpret speedup heterogeneity and source sensitivity. Figure 3's caption nevertheless retains the obsolete synchronization interpretation.

D1.justification: V2 documents regular-expression extraction for Skeleton-of-Thought and exposes raw generation syntax, including the previously unshown <promise> marker, in Appendix G. Core checkpoint, hyperparameters, hardware, and annotation-prompt information remain unchanged. The KV-caching explanation moves to Appendix D without a substantive implementation revision.

R1.justification: The main diffusion and semantic-parallelism positioning is retained. V2 adds token-ordering references and a focused novelty clarification in Appendix E, distinguishing its hybrid definition from Block Diffusion, Eso-LM, and ARDMs, and from continuous-diffusion multimodal hybrids such as HybridVLA and Monoformer. Publication-metadata updates do not constitute additional substantive changes.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and formal exposition are extensively rewritten around denoising order. V1's separate data, training, and inference subsections are consolidated into Implementation; caching moves to an appendix. Terminology changes from spans to chunks, and dense/sparse variant names are reassigned throughout.

P2.justification: V2 expands comparison plots, revises the ablation display, adds two tables and a speedup histogram, and introduces boxed raw and cleaned generation examples. V1's attention-mask figure moves to Appendix H as the sparse variant, accompanied by a new dense-attention diagram. Algorithm 1 is expanded into a full-width annotated display.

improvement.justification: V2 improves empirical support by adding directly relevant semantic-parallelism baselines and revealing performance heterogeneity and a concrete planning failure. These address gaps in v1's comparisons and reliability discussion. The gains are limited by reporting inconsistencies: Figure 3's caption contradicts the revised synchronization results, some Section 5 statements retain obsolete variant associations, and supplementary sample counts are unexplained. Overall, support and transparency improve, but the revision does not establish an unqualified substantial quality gain.
